content.title: Central and Inscribed Angles in Circles
content.overview: This lesson focuses on the geometric relationship between central angles and inscribed angles that intercept the same arc. Understanding this relationship allows you to calculate unknown angle measures within a circle based on the position of the vertex.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between central angles and inscribed angles based on vertex location.
Identify the intercepted arc shared by two or more angles.
Apply the rule that an inscribed angle is half the measure of the central angle intercepting the same arc.

sections.title: Defining the Angles
sections.content: A central angle is an angle whose vertex is the center of the circle. The measure of a central angle is exactly equal to the degree measure of the arc it intercepts. An inscribed angle is an angle whose vertex lies on the circle itself, with sides that are chords of the circle. The measure of an inscribed angle is always half the measure of its intercepted arc.

sections.title: The Central-Inscribed Relationship
sections.content:
When a central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc, they are mathematically linked. Because the central angle equals the arc and the inscribed angle is half the arc, the inscribed angle is exactly half the measure of the central angle. Conversely, the central angle is double the measure of the inscribed angle for that specific arc.

![A flow chart showing the steps to relate central and inscribed angles.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/f4fd03b9-ed43-4832-afc3-57c24d8edb2f-1786506009731-520.webp)

worked_examples.question: In a circle with center O, points A and B lie on the circumference. Central angle AOB measures 110 degrees. Point P is another point on the circle such that angle APB is an inscribed angle. What is the measure of angle APB?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the intercepted arc. Both angle AOB (central) and angle APB (inscribed) intercept arc AB. Step 2: Recall the relationship. The inscribed angle is half the central angle for the same arc. Step 3: Calculate. 110 degrees / 2 = 55 degrees. Therefore, angle APB = 55 degrees.

worked_examples.question: An inscribed angle XYZ intercepts arc XZ and measures 35 degrees. If point C is the center of the circle, what is the measure of central angle XCZ?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Identify the intercepted arc. Both angles intercept arc XZ. Step 2: Recall the relationship. The central angle is double the inscribed angle for the same arc. Step 3: Calculate. 35 degrees * 2 = 70 degrees. Therefore, angle XCZ = 70 degrees.

common_mistakes: Assuming two angles are related when they intercept different arcs.
Confusing the vertex locations: thinking the inscribed angle is the one at the center.
Doubling when you should halve, or vice versa, resulting in an angle that is 4 times larger or smaller than it should be.
exam_tips: Always look for the 'V' shape of the inscribed angle and the 'pizza slice' shape of the central angle.
If the problem doesn't provide a diagram, sketch the circle and label the center and the points on the circumference to visualize the arc.
Check if multiple inscribed angles intercept the same arc; if they do, those inscribed angles are equal to each other.
content.recap: A central angle (vertex at center) is equal to its arc. An inscribed angle (vertex on circle) is half its arc. Therefore, for the same arc, the inscribed angle is half the central angle.

knowledge_claims.content: A central angle is an angle with its vertex located at the center of the circle.
An inscribed angle is an angle with its vertex located on the circumference of the circle.
The measure of a central angle is equal to the degree measure of the arc it intercepts.
The measure of an inscribed angle is equal to half the degree measure of the arc it intercepts.
If a central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc, the inscribed angle is half the measure of the central angle.
If a central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc, the central angle is twice the measure of the inscribed angle.
An inscribed angle is formed by two chords that meet at a point on the circle's edge.
A central angle is formed by two radii of the circle.
To find an inscribed angle from a known central angle on the same arc, divide the central angle by 2.
To find a central angle from a known inscribed angle on the same arc, multiply the inscribed angle by 2.
It is a mistake to treat an inscribed angle as equal to the central angle even if they share the same arc.
Before applying the 1:2 ratio, verify that both angles actually terminate at the same two points on the circle's circumference.

videoLesson.title: Compare Central and Inscribed Angles
videoLesson.description: Recognize which arc both angles intercept and compare their measures. If an angle is inscribed, take half the central measure; if central, double the inscribed measure.
